title: API intake endpoint and API credential provisioning (backend + Settings/broker UI)
objective: Tenants and brokers get OAuth client-credentials for REST lead intake; POST /api/v1/intake/leads enforces credential scoping (broker unspoofable), returns structured errors and non-blocking duplicate warnings; Settings gains the API access tab and broker pages gain credential management (spec FR-25, FR-33, §12.6, §13).
scope: api_credentials table + provisioning/regenerate/disable commands using IKeycloakAdminService
Settings API access tab UI + broker view API credentials section
Rate limiting on the intake endpoint
implementation_details: Liquibase 140-api-credentials: api_credentials (tenant_id, id, broker_id bigint null, keycloak_client_id text unique, status text check in ('active','disabled'), created_by/at, last_rotated_at, disabled_at; PK (tenant_id,id))

Features/ApiAccess: ProvisionTenantCredentialCommand / ProvisionBrokerCredentialCommand -> IKeycloakAdminService.CreateConfidentialClientAsync(clientId pattern 'qiq-t{tenantId}[-b{brokerId}]', attributes tenant_id/broker_id) returning secret ONCE in response; RegenerateSecretCommand; DisableCredentialCommand; GetCredentialsQuery (id + status, secret only via permission-bound reveal action calling Keycloak); all RequirePermission(ApiAccess.Manage) and audited (provision/regenerate/disable/reveal)

Api/Intake/IntakeEndpoints.cs: POST /api/v1/intake/leads accepts client-credentials JWT (azp/client_id claim) -> resolve api_credentials row (active, tenant active) else 403; broker-scoped credential forces broker_id ignoring payload broker (spoof attempt with mismatching broker returns 422 BROKER_NOT_ALLOWED); tenant-scoped credential validates payload broker against active tenant brokers + channel rules; body = intake fields with Owner OPTIONAL (unassigned lead stays New with no accountable owner -> unassigned alert); reuses CreateLeadCommand with source='api', intake_credential_id set; 201 {leadId, leadRef} | 422 problem+json {errors:[{field,code,message}]} | 201 with warnings.duplicates payload (duplicate check never blocks API intake per FR-33)
Rate limiting: ASP.NET RateLimiter fixed-window per client_id on /intake (e.g., 60/min, config-driven)

UI: features/settings/ApiAccessTab.tsx (enable/disable tenant access, client id display, secret reveal-once dialog with copy, regenerate with danger confirm); BrokerApiSection.tsx embedded in broker view page (same controls per broker)

e2e: api-access.spec.ts: enable tenant API access in Settings, reveal/copy secret once, regenerate warns and rotates; broker page provisions broker credential

findings.description: RULING flag 1 (granular permissions vs AC-024/V-024 'ApiAccess.Manage'): ACCEPTED, non-blocking. The endpoint gates every sensitive credential op with the pre-existing catalogued codes (view->list/reveal, enable->provision, regenerate_secret->regenerate, disable->disable), which satisfies AC-024/AC-078's 'backend authz on every sensitive credential op'. Reusing the seeded+mirrored codes is preferable to adding a redundant Manage permission.
findings.evidence: PermissionCatalog.cs:172-177 + All list 304-307; UI mirror permissionCatalog.ts:99-102 and permissions.ts:61-64; ApiAccessEndpoints.cs:35-40 RequirePermission per route; ApiAccessEndpointsTests.Reveal_WithoutPermission_ShouldReturn403 PASS.

findings.description: RULING flag 2 (new IntakeClientCredentials auth scheme, ValidateAudience=false): ACCEPTED, non-blocking. Issuer (ValidIssuer=authority), signature (Authority metadata) and lifetime ARE validated; only audience is skipped, which is appropriate for Keycloak client-credentials service-account tokens whose aud varies by scope. The real authorization gate is azp/client_id -> active api_credentials row -> active tenant at the endpoint, not token validity. The scheme is scoped to /intake only via IntakePolicy and does not touch the default user JWT scheme (which keeps ValidateAudience=true). A user JWT presented to /intake authenticates against the scheme but its azp (SPA client) matches no credential row -> 403; no bypass.
findings.evidence: AuthenticationSetup.cs:79-101 (intake options + IntakePolicy AddAuthenticationSchemes(IntakeScheme)); IntakeEndpoints.cs:41-53 credential resolution; default scheme options 56-71 unchanged.

findings.description: RULING flag 5 (cross-cutting CreateLeadCommand extension: owner->nullable, +SourceOverride, +IntakeCredentialId): ACCEPTED, regression-free. Browser path preserved: CreateLeadValidator requires OwnerUserId when SourceOverride != Api; handler still resolves the accountable-owner assignment + eligibility only when owner is set; Source defaults to Browser and IntakeCredentialId stays null. Ownerless API path yields an unassigned New lead (no assignment row). Leads suite 50/50 green.
findings.evidence: CreateLeadValidator.cs:39-45; CreateLeadCommandHandler.cs:161-178, 255-273; Leads suite 50/50 PASS; Intake_WithoutOwner_ShouldCreateUnassignedNewLead PASS (status 'new', 0 assignments).

findings.description: RULING flag 8 (regenerate invalidates the SECRET but already-issued access tokens live until expiry — no token revocation): ACCEPTED as non-blocking follow-up. AC-024/FR-25 require old SECRETS to die on regeneration, which is proven (old secret cannot mint a token, new one can). Immediate access-token revocation is standard-OAuth out-of-scope and mitigated by short token lifetime. Note as a follow-up if immediate revocation is later required.
findings.evidence: Regenerate_ShouldInvalidateOldSecret PASS (withOldSecret null, withNewSecret not null); KeycloakAdminService.RegenerateClientSecretAsync.
findings.suggested_fix: Future: add token revocation / short-lifetime enforcement if AC tightens.

findings.description: RULINGS flags 3/4/6/7: all ACCEPTED, non-blocking. (3) tenant-credential channel/broker rules reuse the exact CreateLeadCommandHandler validation (single source of truth). (4) rate limit is config-driven (Intake:RateLimitPermitPerMinute, default 60), fixed 1-min window, partitioned per azp. (6) tenant/broker provisioning unified into one ProvisionCredentialCommand(brokerId?) while the endpoint still exposes both routes. (7) API intake supports existing-party only (no inline-party creation) — reasonable scope; FR-33 does not require inline party creation.

Reveal is gated by api_access.view — the same permission as listing credentials — so any principal that can list credentials can also reveal a secret. Reveal IS permission-bound (satisfies AC-024 literally) and RevealSecretCommandHandler does not check credential status (a disabled credential's secret is useless since its Keycloak client is disabled). Non-blocking design note: consider a dedicated/stricter reveal permission if secret reveal should be more privileged than listing.
findings.evidence: ApiAccessEndpoints.cs:38 RevealAsync RequirePermission(ApiAccess.View); RevealSecretCommandHandler.cs (no status guard).
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: introduce api_access.reveal_secret distinct from view.

findings.description: Intake-created leads record source='api' and intake_credential_id on the lead and a lead.created audit entry, but the audit actor is null on the API path (no application user; the actor is an OAuth credential). Acceptable for NFR-02 given the credential id is recorded on the lead itself; matches the Implementor's flagged MINOR.
findings.evidence: CreateLeadCommandHandler.cs:294-304 audit; lead.Source/IntakeCredentialId set 255-256; Intake_WithBrokerCredential_ShouldForceBrokerFromCredential asserts Source='api' + IntakeCredentialId.
findings.suggested_fix: Optional: record a synthetic credential actor label on the audit entry for the API path.

findings.description: e2e api-access.spec.ts (V-024 UI journey) is test.describe.fixme with real bodies, deferred until a seed persona holds api_access.* grants and the broker view page (embedding BrokerApiSection) exists. Deferral ACCEPTED: V-032 and V-078 are integration-only (playwright_triggerable=false) and are fully covered by the passing IntakeEndpointTests; V-024's provision/reveal-once/regenerate/disable are proven at integration (ApiAccessEndpointsTests) + component (ApiAccessTab) level. NOTE: the reveal-once/copy UI affordance and broker-scoped UI provisioning are unproven in live CI e2e until the seed persona is granted.
findings.evidence: e2e_tests/tests/api-access.spec.ts:18 describe.fixme; ApiAccessTab.test.tsx 4/4 PASS; IntakeEndpointTests 9/9 + ApiAccessEndpointsTests 6/6 PASS.
findings.suggested_fix: Un-skip once seed grants api_access.* and the broker view page ships.

FLAGGED AMBIGUITIES (per CLAUDE.md, not silently resolved): (1) Permission: brief/AC-024/V-024 reference 'ApiAccess.Manage'/'apiaccess.manage' but PermissionCatalog already ships (seeded+drift-guarded) finer-grained api_access.view/enable/disable/regenerate_secret and the UI already used api_access.view. Used the EXISTING granular codes rather than adding a redundant Manage (F-044 no-dead-catalog-surface lesson) - ZERO catalog/drift change. (2) Intake auth scheme did NOT pre-exist: added a dedicated 'IntakeClientCredentials' JWT bearer scheme validating the Keycloak realm issuer+signature+lifetime but ValidateAudience=false (service-account token audiences vary by client scope; real authz is azp->active credential->active tenant; a UI/user token's azp never matches a credential so is rejected). (3) Channel-broker-rules source for tenant credentials: reused the EXACT browser-intake validation in CreateLeadCommandHandler (broker must be active + broker-required-iff-broker-flagged-channel) rather than inventing a separate rule set. (4) Rate-limit numbers: config-driven Intake:RateLimitPermitPerMinute (default 60), fixed 1-min window, partitioned by azp/client_id. (5) 'reuse CreateLeadCommand': reused it for persistence via a thin IntakeLeadCommandHandler (broker scoping + duplicate-as-warning + owner-optional wrapper) but had to extend CreateLeadCommand (owner->nullable, +source/+credentialId) because it hard-required a browser owner+user and hardcoded source=browser. (6) ProvisionTenant/ProvisionBroker unified into one parameterized ProvisionCredentialCommand(brokerId?) to avoid duplicated Keycloak/store/audit logic; endpoint still exposes both routes. (7) API intake supports existing-party only (no inline-party creation) this task. (8) Regenerate 'old token rejected': proved old SECRET rejected by Keycloak (can't mint new tokens); already-issued access tokens remain valid until expiry per OAuth (no token revocation implemented). MINOR: intake-created lead audit actor is null (no app user; ActorLabel not settable on CurrentUser for API path) - action+credential still recorded.
